title: Heartbreak in Orono: Maine field hockey falls to UNH in overtime - The Maine Campus
content: ORONO, Maine — The University of Maine field hockey team watched a two-goal lead disappear Friday, Oct. 9, as the University of New Hampshire stormed back to force overtime before scoring the game-winner with just over a minute remaining. This resulted in a heartbreaking 4-3 loss for Maine. Maine entered the contest ranked No. 43 in Division I, with a 5-5 overall record and a 1-0 conference record. The Black Bears were fresh off a 1-0 road loss to Towson University and a 3-1 home victory over the University at Albany. “We went into that game knowing that they were a really strong team, but knowing that we’d been working super hard that week,” second-year forward Martha Barratt said before Friday’s game. “To come away with such a convincing win, I think it has boosted our confidence a lot going into the next few weeks.” Head coach Josette Babineau also praised the team’s performance against UAlbany, highlighting the energy and effort that Maine would need to carry into its matchup with New Hampshire. “We had a very quick start in the game and just kept the energy going throughout,” Babineau said. “The effort was pretty consistent from beginning to end.” On the other side, UNH was only 2-6 but played a remarkably difficult schedule, which helped the Wildcats earn a No. 36 ranking in the Ratings Percentage Index (RPI), making them the highest-ranked America East school. New Hampshire was coming off a 1-0 conference-opening win against the University of Vermont and a 5-0 loss against Miami University in Ohio. Friday’s contest was an end-to-end affair, with a tightly contested first quarter featuring a late Maine goal that put the Black Bears up 1-0. The goal was scored by Barratt. She helped Maine make it 2-0, picking up an assist as fourth-year defender Eloise Penty slotted the ball home in the second quarter. Following halftime, New Hampshire came out looking reinvigorated and opened the scoring in the second half less than four minutes in, as first-year midfielder Delilah Talbot blasted a shot into the net. Maine responded quickly and extended its lead back to two when Barratt scored her second goal of the day. UNH would not let Maine leave the quarter with that two-goal lead, though. A few minutes later, first-year midfielder Sophie Godwin beat Maine’s defense to cut the deficit to one, putting the score at 3-2 in Maine’s favor heading into the final quarter. The final quarter was a back-and-forth affair, and UNH tied the game at 3-3 early in the quarter as Godwin found the net, scoring unassisted for the second time. From there, both teams’ defenses held strong, and the game went to overtime. The defensive battle continued, with neither team able to find the winning goal. With just over a minute remaining, first-year forward Julianna Casucci scored the game-winning goal, allowing New Hampshire to steal a crucial conference and rivalry win on the road. New Hampshire dominated the shot battle, taking 18 shots in total, with 15 on target, compared to Maine’s four shots, three of which were on goal. All three of Maine’s shots on goal resulted in scores against Wildcat third-year goalie Kerigan Ross, while first-year goalkeeper Annabel Halkes made 11 saves for the Black Bears. The loss drops Maine to 5-6 overall and 1-1 in America East play. The Black Bears will look to bounce back Sunday against No. 78 Merrimack (1-9) before traveling to face No. 49 Bryant (6-5) on Friday. After surrendering a two-goal lead against New Hampshire, Maine will need to regroup quickly as it looks to get back on track in conference play.

title: First-Year and Transfer Enrollment Grows Across UNH Durham and Manchester Campuses - University of New Hampshire
content: The University of New Hampshire’s residential campuses welcomed 3,000 new Wildcats this fall, with first-year and transfer enrollment growing across Durham and Manchester campuses. Undergraduate first-year enrollment across the two campuses increased 3.5%, while transfer enrollment rose 11.2%. Overall, there are 4.9% more students in the 2026 incoming class than there were in 2025. “We are thrilled to welcome so many new students this fall,” UNH President Elizabeth Chilton said. “While there are many challenges facing higher education right now, by focusing on a high-quality academic experience, experiential learning, and creating value for students and their families, we are increasingly a first-choice for many.” The incoming class had the strongest academic profile of any incoming class in university history. Incoming students posted an average high school GPA of 3.7. The share of first-year students entering with a 4.0 GPA or higher rose from 27% to 31%. The proportion of Honors College students grew to 14%. Out-of-state enrollment grew 11%, with every New England state contributing at least 10% growth over the prior year. In-state enrollment grew 1.7% despite broader regional demographic declines, reflecting UNH's strengthened position in the New Hampshire market. The university's value-focused messaging strategy appears to have resonated strongly with prospective students: survey data shows that nearly half of enrolling students said UNH was a "much better" value than competing institutions, and 79% rated it a better value overall. UNH awarded a record $40 million in financial aid to incoming students this year, with almost every incoming student — 96% of the entering class — receiving aid. Earlier this year, U.S. News & World Report named UNH the Best Value Public University in New England for the sixth consecutive year, recognizing its combination of academic quality, affordability, student success, and post-graduation outcomes. Even with new student growth, UNH’s undergraduate enrollment is lower than last year, as Spring 2026 saw a large class graduating. “We know we have work ahead,” UNH Vice Provost for Enrollment Management Kim DeRego said. “But our latest results point to clear momentum: UNH is growing its incoming class while strengthening academic achievement and investing more in affordability.” Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. title: Law Student Gets Up-Close Look at New York Fashion Week - University of New Hampshire
content: Grace Lamendola in New York as an intern with The Fashion Law. Grace Lamendola is quite literally completing a law school internship in style. Lamendola, a second-year law student at UNH Franklin Pierce School of Law, is serving as an editorial intern with The Fashion Law, a publication covering the intersection of fashion, business, and law. The opportunity has taken her to the outlet’s headquarters in New York City, where she also recently got to experience New York Fashion Week up close. “There’s something pretty exciting about seeing the industry you’re writing about come to life around you,” Lamendola wrote in a post on LinkedIn. So how did Lamendola land the desirable opportunity? By asking a simple question. “Over the summer, I decided to reach out and ask whether they offered opportunities for interns. Luckily, they did,” she says. “Sometimes getting your foot in the door really does start with simply sending the email.” Her role at The Fashion Law entails contributing to editorial projects exploring the legal issues affecting the fashion and creative industries. She is learning how to turn complex legal issues into copy that is engaging and approachable for readers, and the experience has allowed her to discover just how much legal work takes place away from the public eye to protect brands and influence the fashion world. "I've loved getting a behind-the-scenes look at the legal issues shaping the fashion and creative industries while getting to work on projects that combine two things I really enjoy: writing and law," Lamendola says. The internship brought Lamendola back to her home state. A native of Albany, New York, she chose UNH Law because she fell in love with downtown Concord – and it’s profusion of affordable coffee – on her first visit. She also fell in love with the law school’s vibe. “I loved the close-knit feel of the law school and the sense that I could really make my own path here,” she says. “It’s been a busy, challenging, and rewarding experience so far, and I’ve had the opportunity to explore some pretty unique areas of law.” Throughout he’s had a strong interest in intellectual property law, particularly in trademarks and brand protection, and The Fashion Law internship has allowed her to stretch her skills in those areas while also sharpening her writing and research abilities. “I’m excited to keep growing as a writer and sharpening my legal research skills, but especially to keep learning from the amazing people at The Fashion Law. My mentors have been incredibly inspiring, and getting to learn from people who are doing such interesting work has made me even more excited to keep exploring this field,” Lamendola says. She’s learning skills that she can carry forward when she enters the legal field professionally. And given the subject matter, it’s the kind of internship that doesn’t just look good on paper. “It’s been exciting – and, of course, totally fashionable!” she quips. “I’ve learned how important it is to develop and write in a specific editorial voice, manage multiple deadlines, and turn complex legal issues into writing that people actually want to read.” Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. title: Former UNH star Dylan Laube scores first NFL touchdown - WMUR
content: Former University of New Hampshire star Dylan Laube scored the first touchdown of his NFL career Sunday, reaching the end zone on a 2-yard run in the fourth quarter of the Las Vegas Raiders’ 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. “It’s always a great feeling to come back here to my second home,” Laube told News 9. “I wish we came out with a win, but they played a complete game today. It was definitely a tough one.” Laube said seeing his family, friends and former UNH teammates gave him an extra boost. He said he was disappointed the Raiders couldn’t make the game closer, but said scoring in front of them still felt special. “I wish we won the game and it was a closer game, too, but it’s definitely a great feeling,” he said. Laube also discussed his success with returning kicks for the Raiders and said every year,  proving to be essential for the team is important. “You have to make a statement on every single team,” he said. “This year I carved a role out, and we’ve been super hot.” Laube said he looks forward to taking on the Buffalo Bills next week. title: Earnings Week Ahead: JPM, JNJ, BAC, GS, C, UNH, TSM, and more - TradingView
content: The upcoming week marks the beginning of earnings season, with major U.S. banks, semiconductor leaders, healthcare companies, and asset managers taking center stage. JPMorgan Chase JPM, Bank of America BAC, Wells Fargo WFC, Citigroup C, Goldman Sachs GS, and Morgan Stanley MS headline the banking lineup, offering insight into lending trends, net interest income, trading activity, investment banking, and consumer credit quality. BlackRock BLK, Bank of New York Mellon BNY, and Interactive Brokers IBKR will add perspectives on asset flows, custody services, and investor activity. In technology, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM and ASML ASML will provide fresh signals on AI-driven chip demand, manufacturing capacity, and semiconductor equipment spending. Johnson & Johnson JNJ and UnitedHealth Group UNH bring healthcare into focus, while Alcoa AA offers a read on industrial demand. Prologis PLD, Domino’s Pizza DPZ, Fastenal FAST, Ericsson ERIC and Travelers TRV, alongside regional lenders U.S. Bancorp USB, Truist Financial TFC, PNC Financial Services PNC and M&T Bank MTB, round out a packed slate spanning logistics, consumer spending, business activity, insurance, and credit conditions. Below is a rundown of the major quarterly reports expected during the week of October 12–16. The week starts off relatively quiet, as there are no major earnings announcements planned. JPMorgan Chase JPM is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Tuesday, October 13, following a strong second quarter and upbeat management commentary on trading and investment banking activity. In Q2 2026, JPMorgan reported net income of $21.2B and EPS of $7.70, well above the $5.59 consensus, while managed revenue rose 27.7% Y/Y to $58.0B. Results included a $7.9B gain from the sale of Visa shares and a partial release of credit loss reserves. Excluding these items, EPS was $6.14, and return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) reached 23%. Following the quarter, management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for net interest income (NII) excluding Markets to approximately $96.5B, total NII to $105.5B, and adjusted expenses to $107.5B, while lowering its expected card net charge-off rate to approximately 3.2%. JPMorgan’s Q3 outlook has strengthened following comments from head of trading Troy Rohrbaugh in September that trading revenue and investment banking fees could each increase by a mid-to-high teens percentage Y/Y. This contrasts with Bank of America’s forecast for a decline of more than 10% in investment banking fees. On October 7, JPMorgan also announced the expansion of Chase Payroll, powered by Gusto, extending its business banking services for small and midsize businesses. Barclays maintained an Overweight rating and a $420 price target on October 6, forecasting Q3 operating EPS of $6.02 against consensus of approximately $5.90. The firm also expects JPMorgan to provide an initial 2027 NII forecast of around $103B. Options markets imply a potential move of approximately 4.4% in either direction following the results, above the 10-year average earnings-day move of 3.4%. Wall Street rates JPMorgan a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating is more cautious at Hold. Johnson & Johnson JNJ is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Tuesday, with recent pipeline developments across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience adding to the focus on its pharmaceutical growth outlook. In Q2 2026, Johnson & Johnson reported record revenue of $25.31B, up 6.6% Y/Y, while adjusted EPS of $2.90 topped the $2.84 consensus. Innovative Medicine sales reached $16.4B, up 7.8% operationally, supported by oncology drugs DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, ERLEADA, and RYBREVANT, while SPRAVATO sales rose 40.8% in Neuroscience. MedTech revenue increased 4.5% operationally to $8.9B. Following the results, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance midpoint to $101.1B and lifted adjusted EPS guidance to $11.60-$11.75. Recent clinical developments have added to the company's pipeline momentum. Five-year CARVYKTI data showed treatment-free remission in 50% of patients with early-line relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. TREMFYA also met its primary and major secondary endpoints in the Phase 4 STAR study, while CAPLYTA reported positive Phase 3 results for depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder. These updates reinforce J&J's efforts to expand its oncology, immunology, and neuroscience franchises. Analyst sentiment remains broadly positive. Guggenheim reiterated a Buy rating and $287 price target on October 7, while RBC Capital raised its target to $290, citing pharmaceutical performance, including TREMFYA and Icotyde. JPMorgan raised its target to $285 from $270 while maintaining a Neutral rating. Talc litigation remains a key legal overhang, including a $1.56B Maryland jury verdict that the company plans to appeal. Wall Street rates Johnson & Johnson a Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more cautious at Hold. Also reporting: Citigroup C, Wells Fargo WFC, Goldman Sachs GS, UnitedHealth Group UNH, Domino's Pizza DPZ, Albertsons Companies ACI, and more. Bank of America BAC is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Wednesday, with management's cautious outlook for investment banking fees setting expectations ahead of the release. In Q2 2026, Bank of America reported net income of $9.1B and diluted EPS of $1.21, topping the $1.13 consensus. Revenue rose 19.6% Y/Y to $31.56B, above estimates of $30.78B. Investment banking fees increased 50% Y/Y, trading revenue rose 33%, and return on tangible common equity reached 17%. Management also pointed to continued net interest income (NII) growth, supported by asset repricing and balance-sheet expansion. At the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference in September, CEO Brian Moynihan forecast a decline of at least 10% Y/Y in Q3 investment banking fees to $1.6B-$1.8B from approximately $2B a year earlier. Sales and trading revenue was expected to remain roughly flat against the prior-year quarter's $5.4B. The outlook prompted a 5.1% drop in BAC shares, with trading volume 86% above the three-month average. On October 6, JPMorgan analyst Vivek Juneja lowered his Q3 EPS estimate to $1.12 from $1.16 while maintaining an Overweight rating and a $72 price target. MarketBeat's analyst consensus was Moderate Buy, with an average price target of $63.78. Wall Street rates Bank of America a Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more bullish at Strong Buy. Also reporting: Morgan Stanley MS, ASML Holding ASML, BlackRock BLK, Fastenal FAST, State Street STT, Progressive PGR, and more. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the U.S. market opens on Thursday, with record quarterly revenue already indicated by monthly sales data. Attention is likely to center on the cost of ramping up its 2 nm process, margin trends, and the outlook for continued AI-driven demand. In Q2 2026, TSMC reported revenue of $40.20B, up 36% Y/Y, while EPS of $4.31 beat the $3.82 consensus by 12.8%. Gross margin reached a record 67.7%, operating margin was 60.3%, and net income attributable to shareholders increased 77.4% Y/Y. For Q3, management guided to a revenue of $44.6B-$45.8B, a gross margin of 65%-67%, and an operating margin of 56%-58%, with the anticipated margin decline reflecting the cost of ramping advanced manufacturing nodes. TSMC also raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure outlook to $60B-$64B and increased its revenue growth forecast to above 40% Y/Y from more than 30%. TSMC's latest monthly sales data point to continued momentum. The company reported Q3 revenue of approximately NT$1.49T, up about 39% Y/Y, including September revenue of NT$511.86B, up 54.6%. This puts quarterly sales near the upper end of its guidance range. Industry reports have also pointed to rising customer demand for the 2 nm process family, while Bloomberg reported that TSMC was evaluating a potential semiconductor hub in Texas to complement its planned U.S. manufacturing investments. These developments add to the focus on capacity expansion, advanced-node demand, and the investment required to support future growth. Analyst sentiment remains bullish. Stifel initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $515 price target, while Bernstein reiterated Buy with a $554 target. Morgan Stanley has highlighted the importance of TSMC's 2 nm technology to Apple's upcoming product lineup. Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy consensus on TSM, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating is more cautious at Hold.
